title: CEO Heo Seohong of GS Retail Leads Cemetery Cleaning Volunteer Work at National Memorial Cemetery - 아시아경제
content:
CEO Heo Seohong of GS Retail Leads Cemetery Cleaning Volunteer Work at National Memorial Cemetery GS Retail announced on October 2 that, in commemoration of the 78th Armed Forces Day, it carried out cemetery cleaning volunteer work at the National Seoul Memorial Cemetery in Dongjak-gu, Seoul on October 1. On that day, CEO Heo Seohong and 53 executives paid their respects at the Hyeonchung Tower and then took part in maintaining Section 39 of the cemetery, cleaning gravestones and removing weeds. Section 39 is the final resting place of over 1,100 patriotic spirits, including soldiers who died in the Korean War. Heo Seohong, CEO of GS Retail (5th from the left in the front row), and GS Retail executives are taking a group photo after conducting volunteer work at the National Seoul National Cemetery. GS Retail Since 2019, GS Retail has continued its volunteer work at the National Seoul Memorial Cemetery. Beginning in 2024, the company established a sisterhood relationship with the cemetery and now conducts cleaning activities twice a year in Section 39. Since last year, GS Retail has also expanded its volunteering to the National Daejeon National Cemetery. Park Kyung-Rang, head of GS Retail's ESG team, stated, "Cemetery cleaning volunteer work at the memorial cemetery is a meaningful activity, allowing our members to remember and honor the noble sacrifices of the nation's patriots," and continued, "GS Retail will continue ESG activities that commemorate the significance of honoring patriots and actively practice the values of patriotism." © The Asia Business Daily. title: New BMW F 450 R Revealed With 48hp Twin - brm.co.nz
content: BMW has taken the engine from the new F 450 GS, dropped it into a 175kg naked bike with 17-inch wheels and given it a bit of S 1000 R attitude. And having recently ridden the GS, we reckon the new F 450 R could be a bit of fun. We’ve only just climbed off BMW’s new F 450 GS and came away pretty impressed with it. One of the highlights was the new 420cc parallel-twin, which is smooth, flexible and has a bit more character than you might expect from a 48hp twin. So the news that BMW has taken the same basic engine and put it into a lighter, road-focused naked bike certainly got our attention. The new F 450 R makes 35kW (48hp) at 8750rpm and 43Nm at 6750rpm, with BMW claiming 80 percent of the available torque is already there at 3000rpm. With a ready-to-ride weight of just 175kg, those 48 horses probably don’t need to work too hard. Those aren’t huge numbers, obviously, but with a ready-to-ride weight of just 175kg they probably don’t need to be. Add a short wheelbase, 17-inch wheels and road-focused suspension and the F 450 R looks like it should be an easy bike to get along with – and one you can actually use a decent amount of the performance on a Kiwi backroad. While there’s plenty of F 450 GS underneath it, BMW says the R has been developed as a proper naked bike rather than simply sticking road wheels on the adventure model. The tubular steel frame still uses the engine as a stressed member, but the geometry, suspension set-up and ergonomics have been changed for road use. Wheelbase is a compact 1405mm and it rolls on 17-inch cast wheels wearing 110/70 rubber at the front and a 150/60 at the rear. That’s probably the part we’re most interested in. The F 450 GS already feels light and easy to throw around, so it’ll be interesting to see what that basic platform is like with road-focused geometry, smaller wheels and a lower centre of gravity. The F 450 GS already feels light and easy to throw around, so it’ll be interesting to see what that platform can do on 17-inch road rubber. Suspension is from KYB, with a 43mm upside-down fork and directly mounted rear shock giving 140mm of travel at both ends. The Sport suspension adds adjustable compression and rebound damping to the fork, while the rear offers preload and rebound adjustment. The braking is a bit of a mix, with a single 310mm disc and four-piston Brembo monobloc caliper at the front, with a 240mm disc and ByBre caliper taking care of things at the rear. For a smaller-capacity naked bike, BMW hasn’t exactly been stingy with the electronics, and this is what we found with the GS – it felt like a proper BMW rather than a cheap bike with a BMW badge stuck on the side. Rain, Road and Dynamic riding modes are standard, along with ABS Pro, Dynamic Traction Control, Dynamic Brake Control and engine drag torque control. Riding Modes Pro adds a configurable Dynamic Pro mode on suitably equipped versions. You also get a 6.5-inch TFT display with smartphone connectivity and navigation through the BMW Motorrad Connected app, LED lighting, USB-C charging and heated grips as standard. Seat height is a fairly approachable 790mm, with accessory seats available to drop that by 15mm or raise it by 20mm. BMW’s Easy Ride Clutch (ERC), which we’ve already sampled on the F 450 GS, will also be offered on the R. It’s essentially a centrifugal clutch that automatically takes care of clutch engagement according to engine speed. Combine it with Shift Assistant Pro and you can pull away, stop and change gear without using the clutch lever. BMW has sensibly left the lever in place, though, so you can still use the clutch normally whenever you want to, and with a few of the official photos from BMW showing the 450R rider pulling wheelies, having the clutch lever there is going to be useful… There are four versions of the F 450 R – Base, Exclusive, M Sport and M Sport with Innovation Package. The Exclusive gets Shift Assistant Pro and Sport suspension, while M Sport adds Riding Modes Pro and the familiar M Motorsport treatment. The Innovation Package adds the Easy Ride Clutch (we’re yet to hear which we’ll get in NZ). Styling takes a fairly obvious lead from the bigger S 1000 R, with the same general nose-down, tail-up stance and a suitably angry-looking LED headlight. The F 450 R isn’t about headline horsepower, and that’s probably no bad thing. BMW claims 175kg ready-to-ride, or 176kg with the Easy Ride Clutch, along with a 5.7-second 0–100km/h time and 169km/h top speed. The 14-litre tank and claimed 3.8L/100km fuel consumption should also give it a useful range. Having recently ridden the F 450 GS, we already know we like the engine. Having recently ridden the F 450 GS, we already know we like the engine. It’s got enough shove to be entertaining, it’s easy to use and there’s a nice bit of character to it. Putting that motor into a lighter, lower, road-focused package makes plenty of sense. We’d quite like a go. New Zealand pricing and availability are still to be confirmed, but BMW’s local distributor has confirmed the F 450 R will be priced below the F 450 GS. What do you reckon? title: Global Institute Dialogues: Jason Bordoff on the Geopolitics of Energy - Goldman Sachs
content:
We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Goldman Sachs’ weekly newsletter, offering economic and markets analysis from across the firm. Subscribe now. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. Jason Bordoff is the Founding Director, Center on Global Energy Policy at Columbia University’s School of International and Public Affairs. In this edition of Global Institute Dialogues, Jason Bordoff discusses how the Iran crisis, China’s electrification strategy, and the US shale revolution have changed energy geopolitics. The views stated herein are those of the interviewee and do not necessarily reflect the views of Goldman Sachs or its affiliates. Goldman Sachs is not responsible for any statements made by the interviewee. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has been called the worst oil shock in history. During the Iran conflict, however, oil futures have not yet surpassed their 2008 peak. What does that tell us about the risks that Hormuz poses to the global economy, as well as the sources of market resilience? It is too early to say with certainty what the full oil market effects will be, since the crisis is far from over. But a few things are already clear. Closing the Strait of Hormuz— through which roughly one-fifth of global oil and LNG supplies flowed before the crisis—has long been the nightmare scenario of energy security planning; the head of the International Energy Agency (IEA) called it the largest supply disruption in the history of the global oil market. Yet with the strait almost entirely closed for nearly four months, Brent averaged just over $100 a barrel, up from around $70 when the war began, and peaked at $126 in April—far below the $200 that veteran analysts had warned was possible. Several factors explain the muted response, and most were neither automatic nor guaranteed. Markets were oversupplied and inventories relatively flush when the war began. Saudi and Emirati pipelines, built years ago as insurance, moved over five million additional barrels a day around the strait, cutting the shortfall in Gulf exports to roughly 13 million barrels a day rather than the full 20 million. The IEA coordinated the largest emergency stock release in its history, which, together with commercial draws, offset five million to six million barrels a day. US production and exports surged, and refiners proved remarkably flexible in responding to price signals. Perhaps the biggest surprise was China, which cut imports by roughly five million barrels a day between February and June by halting strategic purchases, drawing down inventories, restricting refined product exports, and reducing domestic demand. The lesson is not that Hormuz no longer matters. It is that resilience was purchased—through years of investment— and that those buffers are now considerably more threadbare and should not be taken for granted. Major energy crises often lead to structural shifts in energy markets. What lasting transformations do you expect the closure of the Strait of Hormuz to create in the global energy landscape? Lasting transformations in the global energy system are hard to predict with confidence. But the energy world had already changed dramatically before this shock: The United States is now the world’s largest oil and gas producer; renewables and electric vehicles have become genuine alternatives in some sectors; a cooperative global order has given way to geopolitical fragmentation; and China, India, and other emerging economies now drive demand growth. The most consequential shift this crisis has revealed is a new geography of energy power. The countries best able to absorb disruption and those forced to bear its costs are no longer the same. The United States weathered this shock far better than it would have a decade ago, given both lower oil use as a share of GDP and much higher production. China, as the largest importer and by far the largest holder of inventories, has come to play an important balancing role in the global market. Meanwhile, the burden of demand adjustment has shifted toward poorer importing countries with thinner fiscal buffers: Jet fuel spot prices briefly approached $200 a barrel in some markets, and dozens of developing economies adopted nearly 200 emergency measures, from rationing and conservation mandates to fuel tax suspensions. Expect a durable turn toward redundancy as countries invest to make the oil and gas system more resilient, not just to move away from it. Infrastructure once considered surplus, such as Saudi Arabia’s East-West Crude Oil Pipeline, proved vital; both Saudi Arabia and the UAE plan to increase their bypass capacity; and Iraq and Kuwait are exploring new export routes. Governments are rebuilding or expanding buffers; the United States should appropriate funds to refill and modernize a strategic petroleum reserve (SPR), now at its lowest level in nearly five decades, while India, South Africa, and Southeast Asian countries are seeking to build reserves and refining capacity. Electrification will accelerate too, but not automatically, and not necessarily in a low-carbon direction without policy direction. China has undergone one of the largest electrification and clean-energy build-outs in history. How is China’s energy strategy evolving, and what does it mean for global energy markets and strategic competition? For more than two decades, China has pursued an energy security strategy built for precisely this kind of disruption. At the core of this strategy is electrification: Shifting the economy away from directly consuming oil and gas reduces exposure to markets prone to geopolitical shocks. The transformation has been historic. More than 32 percent of China’s final energy consumption is now electricity, against 22 percent in the United States and 21 percent in Europe. More than half of new cars sold are electric. China invested $625 billion in clean energy in 2024, nearly one-third of the global total, and clean-energy sectors contributed over 10 percent of GDP in 2025. The Hormuz crisis showed the benefits of that strategy. It was part of the reason China reduced oil imports by roughly five million barrels a day, easing pressure on global markets; China also restricted refined product exports (imposing significant costs on its Asian neighbors), drew inventories, and ceased filling its stocks. If the crisis continues and worsens, with OECD inventories depleted, China’s estimated 1.4 billion barrels of strategic reserves, drawn down only modestly so far, are now among the last lines of defense against a sharper price spike. For decades, US presidents called Riyadh during oil crises to ask for spare capacity; Beijing may come to occupy a comparable position, with comparable influence. The 15th Five-Year Plan calls for China to become an “energy powerhouse,” and Beijing recently raised its 2030 renewable consumption target by 53 percent—which will mean both more renewables and more coal. Paired with China’s dominance of clean energy supply chains—over 80 percent of solar, wind, and battery manufacturing capacity, plus most critical minerals processing—this leaves other countries choosing not whether to depend on imports but which dependence is least dangerous. China’s behavior in this crisis to look out for itself by moving quickly to restrict refined products exports, viewed by some as prioritizing domestic energy security at the expense of neighboring Asian countries, may make that trade-off look less attractive. The shale revolution made the United States the world’s top oil and gas producer. To what extent has that changed the United States’ geopolitical position, and what does the country need to do to maintain it? Combined with lower oil intensity, the shale revolution has fundamentally strengthened America’s geopolitical position, and this crisis demonstrated it. The US economy is nearly four times larger than in 1973, while domestic oil demand is only slightly higher. Two decades ago, the country imported 60 percent of the oil it used; this spring, it became the world’s largest oil exporter and briefly a net crude exporter for the first time since World War II. Oil is globally priced, so Americans still feel higher pump prices. But the broader damage has been far smaller than it once was: Economists at the Dallas Fed estimate a shock comparable to this year’s would have cut US real GDP growth by 5.6 percentage points in 1980, versus roughly 0.3 points today. As a net exporter, the United States saw higher prices transfer income to domestic producers, workers, and shareholders rather than abroad. In an acute disruption, physical barrels can price far above futures benchmarks, forcing import-dependent economies in Europe and Asia to pay steep premiums for immediate delivery; abundant domestic production gave the United States a valuable window of insulation from these dislocations. The contrast was even starker in natural gas, where European and Asian prices moved toward $20 per million BTUs while US benchmarks stayed below $3 per million BTUs—an example of a divergence the economist Lucas Davis estimates has saved American consumers roughly $5 trillion over two decades. Maintaining this position means resisting the temptation to squander it: Refill and modernize the SPR; keep export markets open rather than yielding to calls for restrictions that could damage US credibility and undermine domestic production and refining capacity; and preserve the efficiency, mass transit, and EV policies that reduce oil exposure. America’s newfound position as a dominant producer also means recognizing an uncomfortable corollary—a superpower insulated from the consequences of the turmoil in which it’s involved has fewer reasons for restraint. For investors, what are the most important trends in the energy transition? Where is the market overestimating change, and where is it underestimating it? The most important trend for investors is that the energy transition is no longer driven by climate policy alone. Energy security, industrial strategy, and national security have become equally important and increasingly inseparable. Markets may be overestimating the speed and linearity of the move away from fossil fuels. Every oil and gas shock strengthens the case for electrification, but wanting secure and affordable energy does not necessarily mean moving quickly off all fossil fuels. This crisis, for example, pushed several Asian countries toward coal—Japan allowed greater use of older plants, South Korea lifted limits on coal-fired generation, and India accelerated a $4 billion coal-to-chemicals plan—and the IEA expects record global coal consumption this year. Some governments may also conclude that if the nightmare scenario proved manageable, the practical course is to invest in the resilience of the oil and gas system rather than to move beyond it. Investors should understand both today’s headwinds and its tailwinds for the energy transition. On one hand, clean energy is more capital-intensive, which is especially challenging in an era of higher interest rates. Moreover, in a world of geopolitical fragmentation, governments are shifting from “just in time” to “just in case”: storage, redundant pipelines and ports, strategic reserves, domestic refining, and trusted supply chains. The desire to de-risk from global supply chains dominated by China will lead many governments to feel a growing pull toward energy autarky—the ability to meet one’s own energy needs. The problem is that prioritizing redundancy and domestic manufacturing and extraction is inflationary for clean energy. On the other hand, the drive to reduce exposure to geopolitically risky oil and gas markets will lead many governments to try to reduce imports, giving a push to electrification and domestic sources of electricity, including clean-energy technologies such as solar, wind, geothermal, storage, and nuclear. Electrification, such as EVs and heat pumps, and clean sources of electricity are themselves tools of geopolitical resilience; indeed, energy security, which has returned to the forefront as a policy concern, can be a more powerful driver of clean energy than climate change alone. About the Interviewee
Jason Bordoff is Founding Director of the Center on Global Energy Policy, and Professor of Professional Practice in International and Public Relations at Columbia University SIPA. Bordoff is also Cofounding Dean Emeritus of the Columbia Climate School. Bordoff joined the Columbia University faculty after serving until January 2013 as Special Assistant to President Barack Obama and Senior Director for Energy and Climate Change on the staff of the National Security Council, and, prior to that, holding senior policy positions on the White House’s National Economic Council and Council on Environmental Quality. One of the world’s leading energy and climate policy experts, Bordoff places research and policy interests at the intersection of economics, energy, environment, and national security. He has written prolifically about how to address our greatest energy and climate change challenges and has developed innovative programs and tools to train future leaders to bridge the gap between academic research and policy, focused on delivering research insights in formats and time frames that are accessible and useful to decision-makers outside of academia. title: Bruno Mars Asks Karol G to ‘Dance With Me’ in New Music Video - Billboard
content:
The singer found a way to "get her back" after Drake stole the spotlight with Karol at her Houston concert. Bruno Mars may have just found the perfect way to get Karol G back. Just days after joking that he needed to “get” the Colombian superstar back from Drake, Mars has recruited Karol G for the new music video for his lovely The Romantic track “Dance With Me,” released Thursday (Oct. 1). The video opens with Mars strumming an electric guitar all by his lonesome, pleading the lyrics into a pay phone. Karol is on the other line, sulking in bed in a lace outfit. Mars moves on from the telephone booth to where Karol resides, serenading her from below her balcony with a full band behind him. It’s a dreamy, old-fashioned serenade, with Mars singing to Karol as the instruments flourish. Karol makes her way below, jumping into Mars’ arms as fireworks explode in the sky. The duo stares into each other’s eyes as the video comes to a close, ending the night on a wholesome — and, quite literally, a romantic — note. It’s a fitting visual for “Dance With Me,” which finds Mars leaning into the kind of swooning romance that has become a signature theme within his discography. And Karol G’s appearance comes at a bit of a funny time in their ongoing musical friendship. On Monday (Sept. 28), Mars reacted to a viral video of Drake dancing with Karol G during the rapper’s surprise appearance at her Houston concert. Posting a photo of himself staring dramatically out of the window of a private jet, Mars jokingly wrote, “I have to get her back! I must get her back! I will get her back!” Mars and Karol G already have some musical history together, as the pair teamed up on “Still,” an all-English-synth-pop ballad from Karol G’s sixth studio album, No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto. The collaboration reached No. 41 on the Billboard Hot 100, while the album debuted at No. 8 on the Billboard 200. They also took “Still” to the stage together for the first time when Mars surprised fans during Karol G’s Aug. 15 concert at Los Angeles’ SoFi Stadium. For Mars, “Dance With Me” is the closing track on The Romantic, his first solo album in nearly a decade. The album debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200, while “Dance With Me” opened at No. 42 on the Billboard Hot 100. Your email address will not be published.

The whole world is obsessed with her hit song 'Bby Wow' but are the lyrics about Feid? 2026 is truly Karol G's year. Not only did she become the first female latin artist to headline Coachella but she's also dominated charts with her sixth studio album No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto. The album contains huge collabs with Drake and Bruno Mars but it's her Judeline and Rusowsky collab 'Bby Wow' that's taking over the world. 'Bby Wow' is sung in Spanish but what does it mean and what are Karol G, Judeline and Rusowksy singing about? The phrase "Bby Wow" is actually just English and is just text speak for "baby wow". In the song, Karol G bumps into her ex, reminisces over their relationship and sings about how much she still wants them by their side. title: BMW Motorrad Presents the New BMW F 450 R. - BMW Group
content:
Juliane DreslerBMW Group
            

            Tel: +49-151-601-95733



              send an e-mail Munich. “The BMW F 450 R has everything that defines a true
    BMW naked bike: performance, precision, and pure riding pleasure. It
    is light, agile, and full of character. We have developed a
    motorcycle that inspires confidence from the outset while also
    generating a lot of excitement. With the F 450 R, we are bringing
    our decades-long naked bike tradition into a compact and especially
    accessible format.”
Markus Flasch, CEO BMW Motorrad The new BMW F 450 R: A dynamic naked bike for the 48-hp
    class—developed for maximum riding pleasure and featuring iconic BMW
    design language.
The new BMW F 450 R for the 48-hp class was developed as a
  standalone naked bike within the BMW F 450 model family. The focus was
  on signature BMW riding pleasure, enabled by a carefully engineered
  chassis and geometry layout, rigorous weight optimization, and a
  powerful parallel-twin engine. Its design clearly follows the current
  design language of the high-performance S 1000 R naked bike and
  visually underscores its sporty ambitions. Smooth and characterful parallel-twin engine with a 135-degree
    crankpin offset for dynamic riding pleasure.
At the heart of the new BMW F 450 R is the newly developed
  fuel-injected parallel-twin engine first used in the F 450 GS,
  together with a stainless-steel underfloor muffler. For use in the F
  450 R, it has been specifically tuned for road riding and gives the
  motorcycle a particularly distinctive sound. With an output of 35 kW
  (48 hp) at 8,750 rpm and maximum torque of 43 Nm at 6,750 rpm, the new
  F 450 R delivers powerful acceleration and confident roll-on
  performance. As much as 80 percent of the available torque is already
  on tap at 3,000 rpm, providing strong propulsion from low engine
  speeds. High-tech materials and optimized internal friction make these
  performance figures possible from exactly 420 cc. This makes the
  engine one of the most compact and powerful units in the A2
  parallel-twin segment. It not only meets the stringent Euro 5+
  requirements, but is also particularly efficient, with fuel
  consumption of just 3.8 liters per 100 km. With its 14-liter fuel
  tank, the F 450 R achieves a range of more than 350 km. The service
  interval is the BMW Motorrad-standard 10,000 km. Easy Ride Clutch (ERC) for a significant increase in operating
    and riding comfort.
The optional Easy Ride Clutch (ERC) engages the clutch
  according to engine speed, increasing comfort and control—especially
  in urban traffic, while maneuvering, and on winding country roads. In
  combination with Shift Assistant Pro, it enables riding and shifting
  without manual clutch operation; the clutch lever remains available
  for deliberate rider input. Six-speed transmission and left-side secondary drive. Shift
    Assistant Pro for fast upshifts and downshifts without operating the
      clutch.
The six-speed transmission transfers torque to the left-side
  secondary drive via an X-ring chain. For rapid upshifts and downshifts
  without operating the clutch, the new F 450 R is equipped with Shift
  Assistant Pro in every equipment variant except the base model. It can
  be retrofitted to the base model. ABS Pro, DBC, DTC, and MSR, plus the “Rain,” “Road,” and
    “Dynamic” riding modes as standard—delivering a high level of riding
    pleasure and safety.
The standard “Rain,” “Road,” and “Dynamic” riding modes allow
  riders to tailor the new BMW F 450 R to their individual preferences.
  ABS Pro, Dynamic Brake Control (DBC), Dynamic Traction Control (DTC),
  and engine drag torque control (MSR) are also standard. Chassis with a tubular steel space frame for high rigidity,
    robustness, and riding precision. Naked bike-specific tuning and a
    short wheelbase for agile, playful turn-in behavior.
The new BMW F 450 R also uses the newly developed BMW F 450
  GS chassis concept as its technical foundation, with a setup tailored
  specifically to road use. The tuning focused on easy handling,
  excellent accessibility, and direct feedback. The tubular frame is
  made of welded steel tubes and forged components, with the
  parallel-twin engine integrated as a load-bearing element. Front wheel control via KYB upside-down telescopic fork and
    rear wheel control via an aluminum hollow-cast double-sided swingarm
    with a KYB central spring strut.
At the front, a torsionally rigid 43 mm KYB upside-down
  telescopic fork controls the wheel. On the so-called “Sport
  Suspension,” the fork offers adjustable rebound and compression damping. At the rear, the wheel is guided by a closed, highly
  torsion-resistant yet lightweight hollow-cast aluminum double-sided
  swingarm. It is paired with a directly mounted KYB central spring
  strut with adjustable spring preload and rebound damping. Wheels and tires designed for dynamic riding pleasure.
The new BMW F 450 R rides on lightweight yet robust
  cast-aluminum wheels. The naked bike is fitted with
  tubeless tires measuring 110/70-17 at the front and 150/60-17 at the rear. Powerful braking system combined with BMW Motorrad ABS Pro for
    safe braking, even when leaned over. Dynamic Brake Control (DBC) and
    the dynamic brake light provide additional safety features.
At the front wheel of the new BMW F 450 R, a floating
  single-disc brake with a Brembo four-piston monobloc fixed caliper and
  a 310 mm brake disc provides confident and efficient deceleration. At
  the rear, a single-disc brake with a floating ByBre single-piston
  caliper and a 240 mm disc is used. BMW Motorrad ABS Pro is standard on the new BMW F 450 R. The system
  enables ABS-assisted braking when leaned over, increasing safety in
  corners. Dynamic Brake Control (DBC) enhances safety during braking in
  challenging situations by preventing unintended throttle application.
  The dynamic brake light effectively alerts following vehicles that the
  motorcycle ahead is slowing down. Optimal ergonomics and equipment for comfortable, playfully
    agile riding enjoyment on the road.
A carefully engineered ergonomic triangle and a tapered
  aluminum handlebar positioned high and close to the rider provide an
  ideal riding position in all conditions. The bodywork and the 14-liter
  fuel tank beneath it are shaped for secure support and effective knee grip. The new BMW F 450 R comes standard with a two-piece seat at a height
  of 790 mm, offering most riders an ideal balance of comfort and
  performance. Ergonomics can be customized with Original BMW Motorrad
  Accessories: the high Sport rider’s seat raises the seating position
  by 20 mm, while the low rider’s seat lowers it by 15 mm. The gearshift
  lever, footbrake lever, and side stand are made of forged aluminum.
  The passenger footpeg brackets are bolted to the rear frame—an
  exceptional feature in this vehicle class. Reversible shift pattern for an extra dose of sportiness and a
    true racing feel.
For an extra dose of sportiness, the shift pattern can be
  reversed quickly and with minimal effort—ideal for occasional track outings. Powerful LED headlight and LED lighting as standard.
    Connectivity with comprehensive information and functionality
    through a large, perfectly legible 6.5-inch TFT display. Practical
    USB-C port in the cockpit area.
The new BMW F 450 R comes standard with an LED headlight
  featuring bracket-shaped daytime running light LEDs. The turn
  indicators and taillight of the new F 450 R also use LED technology. The standard 6.5-inch TFT display on the new BMW F 450 R offers a
  wide range of information, brilliant display quality, and intuitive
  operation at a premium level. The TFT display features the Pure Ride
  Screen. M Sport variants with Riding Modes Pro also offer three
  additional Sport screens with detailed information on DTC, braking
  force, and lean angle, as well as a lap timer function. Riders can
  also make phone calls, listen to music, and navigate conveniently
  while riding. Four attractive equipment variants for the new BMW F 450 R.
The new BMW F 450 R is available in four equipment variants. The BMW F 450 R Base is finished in Cosmic Black.
  Also finished in Cosmic Black, the BMW F 450 R
  Exclusive additionally features Shift Assistant Pro and Sport
  suspension. The range-topping models are the BMW F 450 R
  M Sport and the 
BMW F 450 R M Sport with Innovation Package
  (including Easy Ride Clutch), in Snaefell white / M Motorsport,
  including Riding Modes Pro, Shift Assistant Pro, and the Sport
  Suspension. Their white frame and rim stickers in M Motorsport colors
  create distinctive visual accents. What is the BMW F 450 R?
The BMW F 450 R is a new lightweight naked bike for the A2
  licence class, with an output of 35 kW (48 hp) and a road-ready weight
  of 175 kg. How much power does the BMW F 450 R deliver?
The two-cylinder in-line engine delivers 35 kW (48 hp) and
  develops a maximum torque of 43 Nm. What is its range?
With fuel consumption of 3.8 l/100 km and a 14-litre fuel tank,
  the BMW F 450 R has a range of more than 350 km. What is the Easy Ride Clutch?
In combination with BMW Shift Assistant Pro, the rider no longer
  needs to operate the clutch lever when moving off, stopping or
  changing gear. This is particularly practical in urban traffic with
  frequent stops. The clutch lever remains in place and can still be
  used when required. What rider heights is the BMW F 450 R suitable for?
With three available seat heights of 775 mm (low seat), 790 mm
  (standard) and 810 mm (high seat), the BMW F 450 R can be adapted to
  suit riders of different heights. The slim contour below the seat also
  enables most riders to reach the ground very easily. Which licence class was the BMW F 450 R developed for?
With an output of 35 kW (48 hp), the BMW F 450 R meets the
  requirements of the European A2 licence class. Munich, 13 May 2026. Watch the webcast of the public session of the 106th Annual General Meeting of BMW AG.

In August, the PCE fell short of expectations, prompting Goldman Sachs to push back its rate hike to December, and market pricing adjusted accordingly; however, a substantial upward revision to GDP underscores economic resilience, while inflation trends have shown only limited improvement. According to Woofun AI, Goldman Sachs (GS.US), based on August personal consumption expenditures (PCE) data and the latest remarks by New York Fed President John Williams, has officially pushed back its expectation for the Federal Reserve's second rate hike this year from October to December, while noting that the likelihood of ultimately needing no further rate hikes has increased significantly. This revision in the forecast marks a significant shift on Wall Street regarding the trajectory of monetary policy. The underlying rationale is that recent inflation indicators have failed to sustain their earlier improvement, while market‑based measures have remained steady around 3% both before and after the statistical methodology change—still well above the Fed's 2% target. "The New Fed News Agency" columnist Nick Timiraos notes that despite strong readings in June and July, August's data showed no continuation of the disinflationary trend. Coupled with earlier weak PPI and CPI figures, the market had already anticipated this development; thus, the PCE data did not deliver any game‑changing insights but rather confirmed the reality that inflation has been stuck at elevated levels since April 2025, failing to make progress toward the 2% target. Goldman Sachs' economics team, led by Jan Hatzius, explicitly noted in its report that the core PCE price index rose 0.25% month-over-month and 3.01% year-over-year—well below market expectations. This prompted them to lower their forecast for fourth-quarter core PCE year-over-year growth to 3%, a figure significantly below the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) participants' median projection of 3.4%, thereby reinforcing the view that rate hikes will be paused in October and action may not resume until December. At the analyst level, differing institutions exhibit significant divergence in their interpretations of inflationary pressures, reflecting market uncertainty over the timing of a policy pivot. Stephen Brown, Chief North American Economist at Capital Economics, adopts a relatively dovish stance, arguing that core price pressures are slightly less severe than previously feared and supporting the view that the Fed will pause rate hikes in October. He specifically notes that the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA)'s recent revision to the PCE methodology has led to downward revisions in historical core inflation data, with these adjustments collectively reducing core inflation by roughly 0.3 percentage points. Coupled with the downward revisions for June and July, this brings the annualized pace of core inflation over the past three months down to 2%, providing statistical support for a pause in rate increases. However, Sal Guatieri, a senior economist at BMO (BMO.US), offered a more cautious assessment, arguing that the underlying trend in inflation has not shown any substantial improvement. According to data compiled by Woofun AI, although the share of PCE price components with annualized increases exceeding 3% has declined from 54% to 51%, it remains well above normal levels—hardly enough to suggest that the fundamental inflationary trend has been fundamentally reversed. Guatieri emphasized that this structural pressure will reinforce the Federal Reserve's view that further policy tightening is still needed to bring inflation back to its target, thereby offsetting some of the easing expectations stemming from the recent cooling of short-term data. This divergence highlights the complexity of current inflation data: on the one hand, the deceleration in month-over-month growth provides some breathing room; on the other hand, the year-on-year base effect and persistent structural components of high inflation continue to pose a dilemma for policymakers. Market pricing has swiftly captured this subtle shift in policy expectations, yet volatility remains pronounced. According to the CME Group's FedWatch Tool, the market currently assigns roughly a 39% probability to a rate hike in October, down from about 45% prior to the release of the PCE data, indicating that investors have scaled back their bets on the near-term pace of monetary tightening. Meanwhile, the probability of a rate hike in December has surged to 90%, signaling that the market has clearly pushed back the window for tightening. In the bond market, the yield on the 2-year U.S. Treasury note fell sharply from 4.887% to around 4.864% following the release of the PCE data, directly reflecting investors' waning expectations regarding the urgency of near-term Fed rate hikes. However, this downward trend did not persist; yields subsequently rebounded, fully reversing their earlier decline, underscoring that market concerns about persistent long-term inflation remain. Meanwhile, the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield continued to rise, further confirming that long-term interest rates are driven by both economic resilience and inflation expectations. This dynamic shift in the yield curve suggests that, despite a decline in the probability of near-term rate hikes, the market has not yet pivoted fully to an easing bias. Instead, it has repriced both the terminal level and the pace of the hiking cycle, underscoring continued respect for the Fed's "higher for longer" policy stance. The robust resilience of macroeconomic fundamentals provides a solid underpinning for inflationary stickiness, making it difficult for the Federal Reserve to pivot easily toward easing. U.S. second-quarter GDP growth was sharply revised up to an annualized 2.2%, well above the previously reported 1.5%, signaling economic momentum that far exceeded expectations. Both consumption and investment—two key components—outperformed their prior readings; in particular, the critical measure of endogenous growth momentum—real private domestic final sales—was also revised upward to 4.6%, underscoring strong domestic demand. The upward revision in investment largely reflects the boost to growth from AI‑related infrastructure spending, while the higher estimate for consumer spending indicates that, supported by a resilient labor market and a buoyant stock market, households' financial conditions remain broadly sound. In August, consumer spending rose 0.9% month over month, partly driven by higher gasoline expenditures amid rising oil prices, while income growth edged down slightly from 0.3% last month to 0.2%. Meanwhile, the overall PCE price index increased 3.4% year over year, unchanged from the previous month, with month‑over‑month growth accelerating to 0.3%. This set of data indicates that, although the deceleration in the month-over-month growth of the PCE has reduced the urgency of a rate hike in October, robust economic expansion and resilient consumer spending suggest that inflationary pressures will not ease quickly. Consequently, the Federal Reserve must remain cautious in balancing growth and inflation, as any premature easing could heighten the risk of an inflationary rebound. title: 2027 Federal Pay Freeze: How Are 2027 GS Pay Scales with Locality Calculated? - FEDagent
content: The end of the calendar year often brings updates to General Schedule (GS) Pay Scales for the Federal workforce.  Here’s an in-depth look at the essential details for 2027 to help you navigate your compensation and make informed decisions for your financial future. On August 26, 2026, President Trump officially submitted an alternative pay plan. This proposal includes a pay freeze on both base and locality pay for most Civilian Federal Employees. The proposal cited fiscal responsibility and economic conditions. The planned pay freeze does make an exception for Federal law enforcement, proposing a 3.8% raise starting in January, as well as service members, with a 5-7% raise for active military and 3.6% pay increase for other uniformed service members. The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) will determine which law enforcement positions are eligible for the 3.8% raise next year. Federal employees received a 1% base pay raise in 2026, after an initial proposed pay raise, but no locality pay raise. The proposed pay freeze would also leave locality pay unchanged from 2026. There are currently 53 locality pay areas. The United States Office of Personnel Management (OPM) uses three factors to calculate GS pay scales. This system applies to most Civilian Feds under the General Schedule, excluding those covered by Executive and Senior Level Pay Tables. The GS Pay Grade system includes 15 categories of pay ranges. GS-1 is the lowest, and GS-15 is the highest. Jobs are assigned a grade based on the level of responsibility, qualifications, and experience. For example, a position that requires a high school diploma but no experience in that field may be a GS-2 position. A position that requires a master’s degree is usually a GS-9. The GS Pay Step system divides each pay grade into 10 steps. Each step is worth about 3% of the employee’s salary, so the higher the step, the higher the salary. Promotions and seniority-based milestones lead to higher steps. In general, it takes 18 years to move from the lowest to the highest step within a single grade. Locality relates to the region where the employee works. This factor adjusts the base rate of pay for the cost of living in a geographic area. While each position is assigned to a specific grade, and each employee is assigned to a step within that grade, the pay rate will vary by location. This ensures fair compensation in high-cost areas like California or major metropolitan areas. While the system may seem complicated, these three factors help address the most fundamental questions involved in compensating a workforce: ·       The differences between positions in terms of responsibilities, difficulties, requirements, etc. ·       The need to compensate long-term workers for their service. ·       The cost-of-living differences when the workforce is located all over the country. Of the three determining factors, locality adjustments can be the most complicated to predict. The amount of the adjustment is calculated as a percentage rate based on data from the United States Bureau of Labor Statistics Annual National Compensation Survey. This tool gathers data on compensation from government and non-government sectors in locations all over the country. This information is then compared to the base pay of federal employees in similar positions to calculate the locality pay adjustment factor. The Office of Management and Budget (OMB) defines 53 locality areas that OPM uses in setting locality adjustments for all 50 states and all United States territories and possessions. OMB uses defined Metropolitan Statistical Areas and Combined Statistical Areas for this purpose. Hawaii and Alaska have their own pay scales, and 51 other locality areas center on major metropolitan areas. Locations inside the continental United States that don’t fall into an established locality area are grouped as “Rest of United States.” Year over year, OPM recommends changes as needed. The President recommends wholesale adjustments to the pay scales, and they are then approved by Congress each year. Federal employees working abroad are not eligible for locality pay adjustments. How Can I Use the Locality Pay Adjustment Factor Information? Civilian Feds often earn more because of the locality pay adjustment factor. You can find the adjustment rate for your locality by visiting the locality area pay definitions published by OPM. This tool is also useful if you’re considering applying for a similar position in a different part of the country; you can estimate how much higher or lower the pay might be in a new location. One of the most important reasons to thoroughly understand your current and future compensation is to calculate your family’s insurance and benefits needs. title: GS Entec to supply 37 monopiles for Taean offshore wind farm - Korea JoongAng Daily
content: The contract comes as GS Entec works to expands its production capacity to capture growing demand for large-scale offshore wind projects. GS Entec, a major plant equipment manufacturer and subsidiary of GS Global, will supply 37 monopiles to a planned offshore wind farm off Taean, South Chungcheong, as it expands its production capacity to capture growing demand for large-scale offshore wind projects, the company said on Wednesday. Under the contract signed with Taean Wind Power, a joint venture company developing a major 504-megawatt offshore wind farm off the coast of Taean, GS Entec will start production in July 2027 and finish deliveries by the end of August 2028. Monopiles are large steel tubes driven into the seabed to support wind turbines and their towers. According to GS Entec, more than 70 percent of offshore wind projects worldwide use them. The 504-megawatt wind farm is jointly developed by Singapore-based Vena Energy, Danish investor Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners and Korea Western Power. Construction is set to begin in 2028, and completion is targeted for 2030. Once running, the farm is expected to generate enough electricity for about 300,000 households a year. GS Entec supplied all 64 monopiles for the Yeonggwang Nakwol offshore wind project in 2023. This month, it completed a 300 billion won ($220.8 million) plant expansion. The expansion raised its annual production capacity from 40,000 tons to 150,000 tons. “Based on our accumulated technology and expanded production capacity, we will win more orders in the domestic and overseas offshore wind substructure markets and keep pace with the government’s push to expand offshore wind power,” a GS Entec representative said. title: GS ITM Reorganizes SaaS Division…GS Bizple to Go Independent via December Spin-Off - finance.biggo.com
content: GS ITM, the IT services affiliate of South Korea's GS Group, will spin off its Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) subsidiary GS Bizple through a personnel split on December 1. The process involves merging the business unit that was carved out via a physical split two years ago, then transitioning to a structure where shareholders directly hold equity in the newly established company. GS ITM announced on the 1st that it has completed its merger with GS Bizple and will subsequently proceed with a personnel split of the GS Bizple business division. The company explained that this governance restructuring is aimed at enhancing specialization across business segments and establishing an independent growth foundation. GS Bizple is a SaaS and platform specialist established through a physical split in October 2024. It has operated cloud-based HR management solution "U.STRA HR" and integrated ticketing solution "U.STRA TICKET" as its flagship offerings. The company has demonstrated strong growth momentum. After recording revenue of 19.7 billion won (approximately $14.5 million) last year, it is projected to reach 26 billion won (approximately $19.1 million) this year, representing approximately 32% year-over-year growth. The core objective of this restructuring is to separate GS Bizple not merely as a subsidiary but as an independent platform business company. Upon completion of the personnel split, GS Bizple will establish its own fundraising capabilities. Under the physical split structure, GS ITM held equity in the new company, which constrained external investment attraction. Following the personnel split, GS Bizple will be positioned as an independent legal entity capable of directly engaging with investors. Entry into the public-sector software market will also accelerate. GS Bizple expects to secure eligibility to bid on public software contracts under 4 billion won (approximately $2.9 million), which had previously been restricted. This will enable the company to expand the customer base for U.STRA HR and U.STRA TICKET—previously supplied primarily to private enterprises—into the public sector. Following the split, GS ITM will concentrate its capabilities on existing IT services businesses including system integration (SI), system management (SM), AI transformation (AX), security, and internet data centers (IDC). The direction is to separate the operational structures of the SaaS/platform business and traditional IT services business, enabling decision-making and investment strategies tailored to each business's characteristics. Kang Min-kyun, CEO of GS ITM, stated, "This restructuring is a strategic decision to maximize each company's unique capabilities by focusing on their respective core businesses. We will further enhance specialization across business segments to create sustainable corporate value." Lee Yoon-suk, CEO of GS Bizple, said, "We will strengthen our solution competitiveness based on a flexible organizational culture and rapid decision-making system optimized for platform companies. Through market diversification, we will grow into a company that leads the B2B platform market." GS ITM explained that despite this restructuring, there will be no changes to business execution and services for existing customers. Both companies will continue customer engagement in their respective domains following the split. This personnel split also carries significance from the perspective of GS Group's IT services business reorganization. The structure creates a scenario where GS ITM focuses on traditional SI and SM businesses while GS Bizple independently pioneers growth areas in SaaS and platforms. While GS Bizple's projected revenue of 26 billion won (approximately $19.1 million) this year still represents a modest share of GS ITM's total revenue, separating the SaaS business—which is growing at over 30% annually—into a standalone entity creates a favorable environment for future valuation and investment attraction. Following the personnel split, GS Bizple plans to focus on solution enhancement while simultaneously pursuing new revenue sources including public-sector projects. The company is expected to upgrade the capabilities of U.STRA HR and U.STRA TICKET and introduce customized products targeting HR management and ticketing demand from public institutions. Under a contract signed Wednesday at the Seoul headquarters of Taean Wind Power, GS Entec will begin production in July 2027 and complete deliveries by the end of August 2028. Monopiles are cylindrical steel foundations that support offshore wind turbines and towers. They can be used in waters up to about 50 meters deep and are generally more cost- and time-efficient than jacket foundations that use a lattice framework. The shallow waters and thick sedimentary layers off Taean make the area suitable for monopile foundations. The Taean offshore wind project is being jointly developed by Singapore-based renewable energy developer Vena Energy, Danish infrastructure investor Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners and Korea Western Power. Construction is scheduled to begin in 2028 and finish in 2030. Once completed, the farm is expected to power about 300,000 households for a year. The company entered the monopile business in 2022 through a strategic technology partnership with Dutch company Sif. The company is one of the few in South Korea with experience mass-producing and delivering large monopiles from a single domestic plant. GS Entec also completed a plant expansion after investing about 300 billion won ($220 million). The expansion increased annual production capacity from 40,000 tons to 150,000 tons, with the Taean project set to utilize the expanded capacity. title: GS E&C completes land-based salmon farming trial - The Korea Herald
content:
Business GS E&C completes land-based salmon farming trial Busan facility reuses up to 99% of farming water, with full-scale shipments set to begin this year GS Engineering & Construction has completed a trial of its land-based Atlantic salmon farming operation, using its water treatment technology to build expertise for future aquaculture projects. Its subsidiary Eco Aquafarm marked the milestone with a ceremony at the Busan Smart Aquaculture Cluster in Gijang County on Wednesday. GS E&C CEO Huh Yoon-hong attended alongside officials from the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries and the Busan Metropolitan Government. Eco Aquafarm has managed the full production cycle, from hatching fertilized eggs to raising and shipping salmon. The facility combines a recirculating aquaculture system with digital monitoring and Zero Water Concept technology to reuse up to 99 percent of its farming water. Farming Atlantic salmon requires precise control of temperature, salinity and dissolved oxygen as the fish transition between freshwater and seawater. Heat exchangers and precision controls keep water temperatures at 12-16 degrees Celsius during summer, while a central monitoring system tracks water quality and equipment in real time. The company has applied for a patent for an underwater camera system that helps determine when salmon are ready to move to the next growth stage. GS E&C and Eco Aquafarm secured patents for recirculating aquaculture facilities in 2023 and desalination aquaculture facilities in 2025. To strengthen food safety and quality control, Eco Aquafarm completed seafood traceability and HACCP registration last year and obtained antibiotic-free certification for its Atlantic salmon in June. The companies are also working with LG Electronics to improve hygiene at land-based farms and with the National Institute of Fisheries Science on aquatic disease research and preventive vaccines. GS E&C plans to use the technology, operating experience and data gathered in Busan to expand into other land-based aquaculture projects. “We have accumulated the technologies and operational capabilities needed across the entire land-based aquaculture process, from water treatment and fish cultivation to facility operation, by raising Atlantic salmon at the Busan Smart Aquaculture Cluster,” a GS E&C official said. Completed in December 2024, the cluster has an annual production capacity of 500 tons of Atlantic salmon. GS E&C participates as a private-sector operator through Eco Aquafarm, which plans to begin full-scale shipments later this year. title: GS E&C succeeds in land-based salmon farming demonstration - The Korea Times
content: GS E&C CEO Huh Yoon-hong speaks during a ceremony to mark the successful demonstration of land-based farming of salmon at Busan Smart Aquaculture Cluster in Busan, Wednesday. Courtesy of GS E&C GS E&C has successfully demonstrated land-based farming of Atlantic salmon using its water treatment technologies, securing capabilities that can be applied and expanded to future aquaculture projects. Eco Aquafarm, a subsidiary established by GS E&C for land-based salmon farming, held a ceremony Wednesday to mark the successful completion of the demonstration project and showcased Atlantic salmon raised at Busan Smart Aquaculture Cluster ahead of commercial shipments. GS E&C CEO Huh Yoon-hong and officials from the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries and Busan city government attended the event, and tasted the land-raised salmon and were briefed on the company’s farming technologies. The cluster is a testbed facility capable of producing up to 500 tons of Atlantic salmon annually, with commercial shipments set to begin by the end of this year Eco Aquafarm was established in 2020 to develop a new business leveraging builder GS E&C’s water treatment technologies. Since then, the subsidiary has operated the entire farming process, from incubating Atlantic salmon eggs and raising fish, managing water quality and shipments. Eco Aquafarm's facility at Busan Smart Aquaculture Cluster in Busan / Courtesy of GS E&C Atlantic salmon require cold, clean water, making precise temperature and water quality control essential for stable year-round farming. To meet such conditions, Eco Aquafarm uses Recirculating Aquaculture System based on GS E&C’s water treatment technologies, so that the water can be continuously filtered and reused. The facility also applies Zero Water Concept technology, which enables up to 99 percent of the water to be reused, creating a more sustainable environment for land-based salmon farming. Salmon hatch in freshwater before growing in seawater, requiring the hatching and smolt stages to take place in freshwater while adult salmon are raised in seawater. This requires advanced ICT-based smart farming technologies to precisely control water temperature, salinity, dissolved oxygen levels and quality to maintain optimal growing conditions. Based on its cooling and precision temperature control systems, Eco Aquafarm maintained water temperatures between 12 and 16 degrees Celsius, optimal for raising Salmon, even during the summertime. Its Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition system collected, recorded and analyzed facility data through sensors while automatically adjusting equipment based on real-time water quality monitoring. The technologies developed by GS E&C and Eco Aquafarm resulted in multiple patents. The companies secured patents related to recirculating aquaculture facilities in 2023 and desalination-based aquaculture facilities in 2025. They have also filed a patent for technology that uses underwater cameras to determine when salmon should be transferred to the next stage of their growing environment. “By raising Atlantic salmon at the cluster, we have built technological and operational capabilities across the entire land-based farming process, from water treatment to growth management and facility operations,” a GS E&C official said. “Based on the technologies and data we have accumulated, we will continue to enhance the competitiveness of our land-based aquaculture platform.” Nam Hyun-woo has worked as a staff writer at The Korea Times since 2013, mostly covering business and politics. content: Classic car news, hand-picked vehicles, and auction coverage. Choose what lands in your inbox. Some cars get parked because they're broken. Others get parked because someone loved them too much to use them up. This 1989 Nissan 300ZX GS clearly falls into the second camp. Currently listed on Hagerty Marketplace, the Bright Blue Metallic coupe shows just 7,700 miles, wears its original-owner story proudly, and still pairs Nissan's smooth VG30E V6 with the five-speed manual that makes a Z31 so much fun to drive. The Z31-generation 300ZX arrived for 1984 and carried the Z-car name through the rest of the decade with sharp, wedge-shaped styling that still looks right today. Pop-up headlights, a hybrid digital/analog gauge cluster, and available T-tops made it feel like a spaceship compared with the Datsuns that came before it. Buyers could choose the turbocharged VG30ET or, as here, the naturally aspirated 3.0-liter VG30E in GS trim. That naturally aspirated setup is a big part of this car's charm. It's simple, durable, and rev-happy, and connecting it to a five-speed manual delivers the kind of engaging, analog experience that has made clean '80s Japanese sports cars one of the hottest corners of the collector market. If you've followed the rising interest in these cars, you may remember the 21K-mile 1984 300ZX 50th Anniversary Edition we covered, and survivors with this few miles are only getting harder to find. The first thing that grabs you is the color. Bright Blue Metallic (paint code 426) is a wonderfully period-correct shade, and it's matched inside by blue leather upholstery for a head-to-toe coordinated look that screams late-'80s cool. Removable glass T-top panels let you bring the sky inside, while factory fog lights, alloy wheels (swapped for a set of chrome wheels here), and that long, low profile finish the package. According to the listing, the car stayed with a single owner before the selling dealer acquired it. A State of New Jersey new car dealer inspection sticker is still on the windshield, which is the kind of small detail that makes a survivor like this so charming. The clean CARFAX shows initial New Jersey registration starting in December 1989, followed by later Florida and New Jersey registration. This GS came nicely optioned for its day, with power windows, locks, and mirrors, cruise control, air conditioning, a leather-trimmed steering wheel, bucket seats, and an AM/FM stereo with a power antenna. Power steering and disc brakes round out the list. Ahead of the sale, the selling dealer, Vantage Auto, gave the car a tune-up that included new spark plugs, an oil change, and a brake fluid flush. It comes with its owner's manual, a clean CARFAX report, and a clean New Jersey title. Paint meter readings and detailed condition photos are included in the listing's extensive gallery of more than 300 images, so bidders can see exactly what they're getting. Z31s were built in big numbers, but finding one that hasn't been modified, raced, or used up is another story, and finding one with fewer than 8,000 miles is rarer still. title: The Suzuki Adventure Bike That Rivals The BMW GS At A Lower Price - Top Speed
content: Subscribe to the TopSpeed newsletter to never miss an update The adventure bike segment has never been more competitive, yet one name continues to cast a long shadow over every rival: the BMW GS. BMW essentially invented the adventure bike category with the R 80 G/S in the early 1980s, and the GS lineage has carried that benchmark status ever since. The problem? BMW has never been known for keeping prices reasonable. Even the middleweight F 900 GS carries a starting price that climbs well past $14,000 in base trim — and that's before you start ticking option boxes. The good news is that you don't need a German budget to live out your adventure fantasies. Suzuki's V-Strom 800DE makes a compelling case for itself in the middleweight ADV class: a Dakar-inspired machine that pairs Japanese reliability with genuine off-road capability, all at a price that significantly undercuts the BMW. It strikes a near-perfect balance of everyday usability, long-haul comfort, and go-anywhere confidence — without the premium price tag. Here's why the V-Strom 800DE deserves a serious look. Within Suzuki's V-Strom lineup, the V-Strom 800DE is the most off-road-focused model in the family — equally at home on the daily commute and a cross-continental journey. It is powered by a tractable parallel-twin engine, complemented by fully adjustable Showa suspension and long-distance ergonomics. Wrapped in a Dakar-inspired design, the V-Strom can be yours for well under $12,000. That bang-for-buck appeal is only reinforced by Suzuki's well-earned reputation for low running costs and long-term reliability. The BMW F 900 GS, by comparison, starts at over $14,000. That's not to say the V-Strom is perfect, though. The value-focused formula does come with trade-offs. It doesn't produce nearly as much power or torque as the BMW F 900 GS, nor is it among the lightest bikes in the class. It also misses out on some notable features, including cruise control, tubeless tires, and radial-mount brake calipers — which is partly why it's often overlooked in the segment. Look past those shortcomings, however, and you'll find a terrific adventure bike that covers everything you'd actually need your ADV to do, without breaking the bank. Unlike the V-Strom 650 and 1050, the V-Strom 800 uses a parallel-twin engine shared with the GSX-8R and GSX-8S — a pairing that speaks to the motor's versatile character. According to Suzuki, the engine is tuned for smooth, controllable low-end torque while still revving freely to its peak power output. It produces just over 80 horsepower, which is more than sufficient for everyday riding, off-road excursions, and long-distance touring, even if it falls short of the F 900 GS on paper. The absence of a V-twin may give some traditional V-Strom fans pause, but in practice you're not missing much. The engine retains a V-twin-like character courtesy of its 270-degree firing order. It's also notable as the first Suzuki production motorcycle to feature a cross balancer, which enables a more compact, lightweight layout. The result is a powerplant that occupies less space than a V-twin while delivering similar power pulses that enhance traction and strong low-rpm tractability. Parallel-twin, 270-degree crankshaft, DOHC, liquid-cooled Suzuki says the engine is also tuned for good fuel economy, and according to its UK website, it returns just over 53 US MPG in combined conditions. That's respectable efficiency for a do-it-all ADV, and with the 5.3-gallon fuel tank, you can expect a range of over 280 miles between fuel stops. The Suzuki Clutch Assist System (SCAS) and a bidirectional quickshifter round out the package, making gear changes smoother whether you're filtering through city traffic or cruising the highway. The V-Strom 800DE is the most off-road-capable V-Strom currently on sale, and that's where it closes the gap with the F 900 GS most convincingly. It's built around a steel backbone frame tuned for straight-line stability and nimble handling. According to Suzuki, the chassis keeps the bike composed on the highway while remaining easy to thread through trails and forest roads. The one notable downside is a curb weight of over 500 pounds — on the heavier side for the segment. The frame is paired with Showa suspension designed to deliver comfort and performance across all surfaces. Full adjustability gives riders the freedom to dial in behavior to suit their style and load. With 8.7 inches of travel at both ends and the highest ground clearance in the V-Strom family, the 800DE inspires the confidence to tackle obstacles without scraping the engine cases. Showa Linkage-type monoshock, fully adjustable, 8.7 in. travel Dual 310mm discs with Nissin two-piston floating calipers A 21-inch front spoke wheel makes the V-Strom 800DE even more off-road capable, providing better stability on trails and a smoother ride on broken pavement. The 17-inch rear spoke wheel handles grip and comfort at the back. Both wheels are shod in Dunlop Trailmax Mixtour tires with a semi-block pattern that balances off- and on-road traction. Braking duties are handled by a pair of Nissin axial-mount calipers up front and a single unit at the rear. One look at the V-Strom 800DE and its new-generation Suzuki identity is unmistakable — the aggressive, mass-forward design is sharp and contemporary, and it looks particularly striking in the Champion Yellow No. 2 colorway. The Glass Sparkle Black option is equally appealing for those who prefer a more understated look. Either way, Suzuki says the modern styling draws inspiration from the legendary DR-Z Dakar racer and the DR-Big dual sport, with a focus on long-distance comfort and off-road ease. The wide, tapered handlebar is cast in strong yet flexible aluminum, allowing it to absorb shock during off-road riding. The wider grips are designed to remain comfortable in a variety of conditions, including when standing on the pegs. Speaking of which, the footpegs are broad and fitted with vibration-dampening rubber inserts that can be removed for extra grip on the trails. Suzuki says the seat is both supportive and narrow, keeping it comfortable over long distances while remaining accessible for a wide range of rider heights. The front cowl and windscreen are wind-tunnel tested to reduce buffeting on the rider while maximizing visibility from the saddle. The windshield is adjustable across three positions, though you'll need a hex tool to undo and redo the four screws each time. That's a genuine miss on Suzuki's part — most rivals offer tool-free windscreen adjustment. On the plus side, the clutch and brake levers can be adjusted without any tools at all. The V-Strom 800DE's electronics suite is where the bike's budget-conscious nature is most apparent. The package centers on a 5-inch TFT display — smaller than what the F 900 GS offers — and the Suzuki Intelligent Ride System (S.I.R.S.), which bundles traction control, rider modes, a quickshifter, easy start, and low RPM assist. Notably absent are a six-axis IMU and cruise control, even as optional extras. Suzuki partially compensates with a solid range of Genuine Suzuki Accessories, including side and top cases, an engine guard, center stand, low and high seat options, heated grips, and auxiliary lamps. There's also the V-Strom 800DE Adventure variant, which adds a durable aluminum bash plate and aluminum panniers as standard equipment. For context, the BMW F 900 GS offers a more extensive optional extras catalog, including Keyless Ride, TPMS, Sport suspension, a high windscreen, the BMW Motorrad ConnectedRide Navigator, and more. It's clear that the V-Strom 800DE is a more straightforward package than the BMW GS — but holding that against it misses the point entirely. The V-Strom isn't trying to dazzle you with outright performance or a long features list. Instead, it's built to nail the fundamentals of a middleweight adventure bike: friendly power delivery, long-distance comfort, genuine off-road ability, and essential rider aids. It's a solid ADV that gives you everything you actually need, without charging you for the bells and whistles you may never use. We want to hear from you. In 29 games with the Rumble Ponies, he posted a wRC+ of 158- and that takes into account a little lull that he had in September; remove those 7 games, and he had a 202 wRC+ against Eastern League pitchers. Early on in the season, Voit began working with his hitting coaches to refine his decisions at the plate and to focus on swinging at good pitches and making good contact, putting extra effort into studying scouting reports and figuring out how to get pitchers to work to his strengths rather than him falling into their pitching traps. title: Wide Open GS Title Battle Entering Road Atlanta Finale - Sportscar365
content: Forty-five cars set for Friday’s season-ending Fox Factory 120 at Michelin Raceway Road Atlanta… Under the current IMSA Michelin Pilot Challenge points structure introduced in 2021, there’s been an 80 percent hit rate of drivers leading the points at the second-to-last race and securing the championship at the Michelin Raceway Road Atlanta season finale. The two times out of ten it didn’t happen, the lead was 30 points or less. First-time 2026 GS championship leaders Austin Krainz and Stevan McAleer in the No. 27 AutoTechnic Racing BMW M4 GT4 EVO come to the Fox Factory 120 with a lead of exactly 30 points. Krainz and McAleer haven’t won but have been the model of consistency for two years straight. They can only clinch outright with a win; otherwise, they’ll need to finish ahead of their rivals. This year, they’ve finished between second and 11th in eight of nine races, and only have a worst result of 17th. They’re the fifth different GS entry to lead the championship this year, following the No. 71 Rebel Rock Racing Aston Martin Vantage GT4 Evo, No. 57 Winward Racing Mercedes-AMG GT GT4, No. 95 Turner Motorsport BMW M4 GT4 EVO and No. 13 McCumbee McAleer Racing Ford Mustang GT4. Emblematic of the topsy-turvy nature of 2026, Krainz and McAleer’s pre-Michelin Raceway point total of 2,190 points is the lowest entering the final round by any GS leader since the current points system was introduced. They’re ahead of the aforementioned No. 95 Turner BMW featuring past GS champions Dillon Machavern (2017) and Luca Mars (2025) by 30 points and Robert Noaker in the No. 13 MMR Ford by 40. Both Turner and MMR have second entries this race, including MMR’s debuting No. 61 Ford Mustang GT4 of Jenson Altzman and Erik Evans. Fourth-placed Michael Cooper and Moisey Uretsky (120 back, No. 44 Ibiza Farm Motorsport McLaren Artura GT4) and fifth-placed Bryce Ward (130 back, No. 57 Winward Mercedes-AMG) are in with a mathematical shot. Cooper and Uretsky won both at Indianapolis last race and Michelin Raceway last year. Wild point swings can occur with up to a maximum 340-point swing between first (350 points) and 30th (10). The only GS second-place entry to leap to first at the finale in the last five years occurred in 2021. Jan Heylen and Ryan Hardwick won the finale aboard Wright Motorsports’ No. 16 Porsche 718 Cayman GT4 Clubsport RS, which propelled Heylen from 30 points down entering the finale to the championship by 190 points over Turner Motorsport’s Machavern and Bill Auberlen and Machavern, who had a fraught finale en route to 18th in their No. 95 BMW M4 GT4. Subsequent leaders have held leads of 160, 60, 110 and 100 points in GS the last four years and have brought it home. TCR should have no such challenges this year. Mason Filippi and Bryson Morris entered Indianapolis with a 260-point lead in their No. 33 Bryan Herta Autosport Hyundai Elantra N TCR and left it with a 200-point margin over teammates Denis Dupont and Preston Brown in the similar No. 76 Herta Hyundai. That puts them well in line with past champions who entered the finale with 230, 100, 20 and 100-point gaps and then brought it home. Only last year did TCR see a last-race points change. MMG’s No. 93 Honda Civic FL5 TCR of LP Montour and Karl Wittmer had a race fraught with mechanical maladies, opening the door for Harry Gottsacker to overcome a 10-point – or one position – points deficit and claim his second TCR title (2023). Provided Filippi and Morris start the season finale, they’ll score at least last-place points and have enough in hand to wrap the title, which would extend Herta and Hyundai’s run of title form where both team and manufacturer have won six TCR titles in the last seven years. Hyundai has won the last six manufacturer titles (2020 through 2025) and all driver titles since 2019, except 2024. It’d be a first for both drivers, though. As for the race itself, four different TCR brands have won at Road Atlanta in the last five years. All of Alfa Romeo, Honda, Hyundai and Cupra have won since 2021. There are 45 cars entered for the finale, split 31 GS and 14 TCR. Pilot Challenge teams practice Wednesday, September 30 and Thursday, October 1 with qualifying Thursday evening at 6:25 p.m. ET. The FOX Factory 120 streams live on Friday, October 2, at 11:35 a.m. ET on Peacock and live, flag-to-flag, ad-free courtesy of Michelin on the IMSA Official YouTube channel. title: GS Stock Edges Higher Premarket: Goldman Sachs Reportedly Weighs John Waldron As Next CEO - TradingView
content: Shares of Goldman Sachs Group, Inc.. (GS) edged 0.17% higher in the premarket session early Tuesday after reports suggested the bank is considering a plan for David Solomon to step down as CEO and be replaced by Chief Operating Officer John Waldron. According to a report from The Wall Street Journal, which cited people familiar with the matter, the move could come as soon as next year. According to the report, discussions have considered Waldron taking over as CEO around the end of 2027 or in 2028. Waldron currently serves as the bank’s president and COO. Waldron joined Goldman Sachs in 2000. Meanwhile, per current discussions, CEO Solomon is likely to stay on the board as executive chairman for about one to two years after stepping down as CEO, the report noted. The bank has been working over the past year to transition duties related to Waldron’s COO role to its finance chief, Denis Coleman, according to the report. The plan will need to be approved by Goldman’s board, which is likely to happen in the coming months, according to some people familiar with the matter. However, they added that the timing of the leadership transition may be fluid and is subject to change. Waldron’s promotion to CEO would leave the position of president open, although as per the people in the report, it is currently not clear how this will play out. The report said a big part of the problem would be the risk of top executives leaving the firm if they don’t get the title. Reuters cited those executives including the co-heads of the firm’s global banking and markets division Dan Dees and Ashok Varadhan, and Marc Nachmann, global head of asset and wealth management. Before the report on the CEO transition, HSBC raised its price target on Goldman Sachs to $1,007 from $995 and maintained a ‘Hold’ rating on the shares, according to The Fly. The revised target implies an upside of nearly 10% from the company’s last close. The analyst said that it had adjusted targets in the banks and brokers space as part of a third-quarter earnings preview, noting that bank investor sentiment had reversed amid rising global yields and renewed fiscal concerns. HSBC said that it sees the banking sector's year-over-year earnings growth moderating due to tougher capital market comparables and higher costs, adding that it prefers banks with opportunities to improve return on equity that are trading at "undemanding" multiples. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around GS stock was ‘bullish’ at the time of writing. One user said, “$GS Baffling how this can be held down for so long. Clearly the top investment banking company in the world. Such cheap prices, you have to believe this is the time to get rid of weaker hands to get shares for an ER that will send this on an upward trajectory again.” Another user said, “$GS Give me a break! This stock is great for growth. GS can’t possibly lose long term with the huge amount of capital they “manage” for constant $ $ $.” GS stock has gained about 14% in the last one year.
